newsitem.title: USA: IBM to shut down World Avenue.
newsitem.headline: IBM to shut down World Avenue.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp. said Tuesday it will close down its virtual shopping mall on the Internet, called World Avenue, as of July 9, due to low traffic.
The Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday that IBM is preparing to shut down the virtual shopping mall.
An IBM spokesman said the computer giant did not want to market to the customers of its customers -- stores with locations at the site -- in order to generate traffic to the shopping site.
"One piece that stood out and that was counter to our strategy was drawing consumers to the site," he said.
"For us to be marketing to their customers was at odds with our strategy," the IBM spokesman said. "It requires a significant ongoing investment."

The mall, which can be found at www.worldavenue.com, currently has three computer stores (two are IBM's); two department stores, Gottschalks Inc. and Hudson's Bay Co.; eight other speciality stores; and five sports areas selling sporting events tickets and merchandise.
IBM declined to say how much it has invested in the site, which it announced last June and debuted last autumn. IBM said at the time it received a start-up fee from its vendors.

The start-up fee was estimated at around $30,000. IBM also received a $2,500 monthly maintenance fee to maintain the sites and a 5 percent commission on transactions. IBM said it did not have any specific numbers about site traffic.
"Obviously, it wasn't where we wanted it to be," the spokesman said.

IBM said it will continue to build Web sites, manage them, run them and service them for its customers. "Our role is to serve as the IT (information technology) enabler and partner," IBM said. IBM still believes that electronic malls can survive on the Internet, if they are marketed by the retailers.
Separately, IBM unveiled an enhanced version of its VoiceType Simply Speaking dictation software, which allows people to operate a computer with their voice instead of a keyboard and a mouse.
The new software, called Simply Speaking Gold, costs $99. IBM plans to ship the software in Spanish, French, German, Italian, and British English in July.
IBM said its VoiceType Simply Speaking product would now be priced at $49.95.
It said it also unveiled ViaVoice, a general-purpose continuous-speech dictation product that recognises the spoken word. ViaVoice will be available in August at a price of $199.
